messages.body: Hi - I was charged $49 twice this month for my Pro plan. Order refs 88412 and 88530. Can you refund the duplicate? Also, please tell me why it happened, I don't want it recurring next month.

context: Account shows two successful charges of $49 on the same billing cycle, refs 88412 and 88530.
Ref 88530 was created by a retry after a webhook timeout and is a confirmed duplicate.
Duplicate charges are refunded in full once confirmed; no approval needed from the customer.
Refunds post to the original card in 5-10 business days depending on the bank.
The webhook retry bug was fixed in the 12 Mar release; it cannot affect future cycles.
Support cannot change a customer's billing date.
issues: explain the cause and confirm it won't recur
ideal_reply:
Hi,

Thanks for flagging this, and sorry for the trouble. I've confirmed ref 88530 is a duplicate - it was created by a retry after a webhook timeout on our side - and I've issued a full $49 refund. It should land on your original card within 5-10 business days, depending on your bank.

On the cause: the retry bug behind it was fixed in our 12 March release, so it won't affect your next cycle.

You don't need to do anything else. If the refund hasn't shown up after 10 business days, reply here and I'll chase it with our payments team.

Best,
Support

messages.body: I'm having trouble with the new update. It keeps crashing when I try to open it.

context: Customer reports the app crashes on launch after the latest update.
A known bug in the update causes this issue.
The app needs to be restarted to clear the error.
ideal_reply:
Hi,

I'm sorry to hear about the crash with the new update. This is a known issue that we're working on fixing. In the meantime, you can try restarting the app to clear the error.

We'll keep you updated on the progress of the fix.

Best,
Support

messages.body: We just signed up - 12 people on the team. Two things before we roll it out: can we bring across our old Zendesk tickets, and can I set it up so tickets from our billing@ address only go to our finance folks? Trying to get this live by end of next week.

context: The Zendesk importer brings across tickets, their comment threads, and requester email addresses.
The importer does not bring across Zendesk macros, tags, or custom field definitions.
Imports are queued and typically finish within 24 hours; larger accounts can take longer.
Shared inboxes support per-inbox access, so a billing@ inbox can be limited to a chosen set of users.
Rules can auto-assign incoming email based on the receiving address.
The account is on the Growth plan, which includes 5 shared inboxes.
issues: whether Zendesk tickets can be migrated and what comes across
restricting the billing@ inbox to the finance team
ideal_reply:
Hi,

Welcome aboard - both of these are doable, and comfortably inside your timeline.

On the migration: our Zendesk importer brings across your tickets, their full comment threads, and requester email addresses. Worth knowing up front that macros, tags and custom field definitions don't come across, so if you rely on those you'll want to recreate them here. Imports are queued and usually finish within 24 hours, though it can run longer for bigger accounts.

On billing@: yes. Set it up as its own shared inbox and grant access only to your finance folks - your Growth plan includes 5 shared inboxes, so you've got room. You can also add a rule that auto-assigns anything arriving at that address straight to them.

If you want, kick off the import early next week and I'll keep an eye on it so you're not waiting on it at the deadline. Just reply here and I'll get it queued.

Best,
Support

messages.body: Hey, we need to move all our stuff over before Monday. Can you help us get it in?

context: The account was created 2 days ago and has no imports on record.
Importers exist for Zendesk, Freshdesk, and Gmail label exports.
Each importer needs different credentials, so the source system has to be known before anything can start.
A CSV path exists for sources without a dedicated importer, but it carries contacts only, not conversation history.
Imports are queued and typically finish within 24 hours.
Support cannot begin an import without either admin credentials for the source system or an exported file.
issues: work out what is being migrated and from where
get the migration started in time for Monday
ideal_reply:
Hi,

Happy to help, and Monday is realistic - imports usually finish within 24 hours once they're queued.

Before I can start it, though, I need to know what we're moving and where it's coming from. Could you tell me:

1. Which system you're moving off - we have dedicated importers for Zendesk, Freshdesk, and Gmail label exports.
2. Whether you need conversation history, or just your contacts.

That second one matters: if your source isn't one of the three above, we can still bring your contacts across via CSV, but historical conversations won't come with them - so it's better to know now than on Sunday.

Send those over and I'll tell you exactly what credentials or export file we need next.

Best,
Support

messages.body: My laptop won't connect to the VPN since yesterday afternoon. It just sits at 'authenticating' then times out. I'm on-site with a client Thursday and I need file share access there.
Thanks - can you confirm whether you've changed your password recently, and whether you're on the ML-4402 or ML-5100 model?
Password changed Tuesday morning as prompted. Laptop is ML-4402.

context: A known issue causes the VPN client to cache stale credentials after a password change, affecting ML-4402 units.
The fix is to clear the saved credential in the VPN client and re-authenticate; instructions are in the internal KB article VPN-14.
If clearing the credential fails, the unit needs a client reinstall, which requires a support session and takes about 30 minutes.
IT cannot provide file share access outside the VPN.
Offline copies of a share can be prepared in advance if requested at least one business day ahead.
Today is Tuesday.
issues: ensure file share access is available on-site Thursday
ideal_reply:
Thanks - that lines up with a known issue. On ML-4402 units, the VPN client can hold on to the old credential after a password change, which produces exactly the hang you're seeing.

First thing to try: clear the saved credential in the VPN client and re-authenticate. The steps are in KB article VPN-14. That resolves it in most cases.

If it still times out after that, the client needs reinstalling. That takes about 30 minutes with me on a session - so if the KB steps don't work, grab a slot with me tomorrow rather than Thursday morning.

One thing I should flag: I can't get you file share access without the VPN working, so as a backstop I can prepare offline copies of the shares you need. That needs a day's notice, so if you tell me which shares by end of tomorrow you'll be covered either way.

Thanks,
IT

messages.body: I've got 6 days of leave left this year and I'd like to take the week of 22 December. Also, can I roll the leftover into next year? A couple of people on my team said they've done that before.

context: The employee has 6 days of accrued leave remaining in the current year.
The week of 22 December contains 3 working days; the rest are company holidays.
Leave requests are submitted in the HR portal and approved by the employee's manager, not by HR.
Company policy allows a maximum of 2 days to be carried into the following year.
Carryover must be used by 31 March or it is forfeited.
Exceptions to the carryover cap require director sign-off and are granted only for leave cancelled at the company's request.
issues: confirm whether unused leave can be carried over
ideal_reply:
Hi,

Good timing on that week - only 3 of those days are working days, the rest are company holidays, so the week of 22 December costs you 3 of your 6 remaining days.

To book it, put the request through the HR portal. It goes to your manager for approval rather than to me, so worth giving them a heads-up if it's a busy period.

On carryover: you can carry a maximum of 2 days into next year, and they need to be used by 31 March or they're forfeited. So of the 3 days you'd have left after December, 2 can come with you and 1 would need using before year end. I know colleagues sometimes carry more - that needs director sign-off and is only granted where the company cancelled someone's leave, so I can't extend it here.

If you'd rather not lose that day, happy to help you find somewhere to put it.

Best,
HR

messages.body: Hi, I interviewed for the Backend Engineer role on 14 May - that's just over three weeks ago now and I haven't heard anything. Could you let me know where I stand, and if I'm out, whether you can share what let me down? Happy to reapply later if so.

context: The candidate completed a technical interview for Backend Engineer on 14 May.
The role is on hold pending headcount approval; no hiring decision has been made for any candidate.
Headcount decisions are expected within two weeks but are not confirmed.
Company policy is not to share individual interview feedback with external candidates.
Candidates may reapply to any role after 6 months.
Recruiting cannot indicate a candidate's ranking relative to others.
issues: explain the current status of the application
respond to the request for interview feedback
ideal_reply:
Hi,

Thanks for following up, and apologies for the silence - three weeks with no word is longer than you should have had to wait.

Here's where things actually stand: the Backend Engineer role is currently on hold while we get headcount approved. No decision has been made about you or anyone else who interviewed. I'd expect clarity within about two weeks, though I can't promise that date since it isn't mine to set.

On feedback - I'm afraid we don't share individual interview feedback with candidates outside the company. I realise that's an unsatisfying answer when you've asked directly, so I won't dress it up as anything other than policy.

What I can do is come back to you as soon as the headcount decision lands, either way. And if it does end up a no, you're welcome to reapply to any role after 6 months.

Best,
Recruiting

messages.body: Following up on my application - any update? Also I wanted to check whether the role is remote.

context: Three open roles currently accept applications: Backend Engineer, Support Lead, and Account Executive.
The sender's email address does not match any application on file.
Applications are tracked by the email address used to apply, so a different address cannot be located.
Backend Engineer and Support Lead are remote within EU time zones; Account Executive is hybrid, 3 days on-site in Berlin.
Recruiting cannot disclose application status to an address that does not match the application on file.
issues: locate the application and give a status update
answer whether the role is remote
ideal_reply:
Hi,

Happy to look into it - I just need a bit more to go on. I can't find an application under the address you've written from, and we track applications by the email used to apply, so it may have come in under a different one. Could you let me know which address you applied with, and which role you applied for?

On remote working, I can answer that now, since it varies by role:

- Backend Engineer and Support Lead are remote within EU time zones.
- Account Executive is hybrid - 3 days a week on-site in Berlin.

Once you send over the address you used, I'll pull up your application and come back with a status.

Best,
Recruiting

messages.body: We've been using this a couple of weeks now and honestly I'm not sure we've set it up the smart way. Is it normal for everyone to be in every inbox? Feels chaotic but maybe that's just how teams do it.

context: The account has 4 shared inboxes and all 9 users have access to all of them.
issues: respond to the concern about how access is set up
ideal_reply:
Hi,

It's not unusual - plenty of teams start with everyone in everything, especially in the first few weeks when you're still working out who handles what. It's not chaotic so much as undifferentiated, and it tends to get noisy as volume grows rather than being a problem on day one.

For what it's worth, you've got 4 shared inboxes and all 9 users in each. The teams that settle fastest usually narrow that down so people only see the inboxes they're accountable for - it cuts the noise and makes it obvious who's picking things up.

No need to do it all at once. If you tell me roughly how your team splits up, I'm happy to suggest where I'd draw the lines.

Best,
Support
